newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. envoy meets leader of Angola's UNITA.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy meets leader of Angola's UNITA.

text.p: The top U.N. representative in Angola said on Friday that the next few days would determine the fate of the country's fragile peace process.

"In the coming days we will know whether we are out of the current crisis," special representative Alioune Blondin Beye told a news conference after meeting Jonas Savimbi, leader of the rebel-turned-opposition movement, UNITA.

Beye and representatives from the three observer nations to Angola's long peace process, the United States, Portugal and Russia, travelled on Friday to the central highlands city of Bailundo to see Savimbi.
Beye said UNITA must show progress in the next few days on a number of issues where it is slacking in its compliance with a 1994 peace deal with the government that ended two decades of civil war.
These include handing over some of the vast territory it controls to the government, defining the number of UNITA troops still under arms, and halting the harassment of U.N. personnel.
A Security Council resolution of June 30 gave the former rebels until August 15 to comply with a series of demands including the ones Beye addressed.
The last few weeks have seen heightened military activity including an army offensive into UNITA-held territory in the country's north east.
"The moment has come for UNITA to answer these questions in a concrete form," said Beye.
One official close to the peace process said Savimbi had agreed to all the issues Beye brought up and had promised to meet with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
"He (Savimbi) basically agreed to everything and to a meeting with dos Santos," said the official. "He said he needs a week to get everything in place, but he is ready to comply."

But the official, reflecting a widespread opinion among those close to the peace process that Savimbi often makes promises he does not keep, said "but these are just words, only words and nothing else".
